newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan leader approval ratings plummet - poll.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan leader approval ratings plummet - poll.

text.p: Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera's popularity has plunged further with approval ratings now at 20 percent, according to an opinion poll released Thursday.

The Datanalisis private poll published in the daily El Nacional said 20.1 percent of 1,000 people questioned were satisfied with the 80-year-old leader, down from over 61 percent in June 1994, four months after he took office.
The poll, conducted from September 12-27 with a five percent margin of error, said that 84.9 percent of respondents thought the country's situation was "very bad".
With annual inflation at a record 115 percent, Venezuela is slowly emerging from recession amid the implementation of an IMF-inspired economic adjustment program.

The survey also showed that former Miss Universe Irene Saez remained the country's most popular politician. Nearly 41 percent said they would vote for the 33-year-old former beauty queen. The next presidential election is scheduled for December 1998.

Saez, mayor of Chacao municipality in Caracas, has not ruled out a bid for the presidency. Critics say she lacks experience, has no real political platform, and that her popularity would fizzle if she were to leave Chacao, which has been nickamed "Irenelandia."
